title: Wisdom and the New Testament language of Divine Wisdom
subtitle: Wisdom → Hebrews / Paul / John
summary: A guided path through Edition 1 relationships in which Wisdom language is placed beside New Testament language about Christ, creation, divine Wisdom, radiance, and the Word. These links identify study relationships; they do not by themselves prove quotation or literary dependence.
items: Christ as “the wisdom of God” is a natural comparison point with Wisdom’s portrait of divine Wisdom.
Compare Wisdom’s imagery with Hebrews’ description of the Son.
Edition 1 preserves a Douay-Rheims cross-reference here; compare the radiance/image language carefully.
Creation through divine Wisdom can be studied alongside John’s creation-through-the-Word language.
A thematic path concerning knowledge of God and eternal life.

title: The persecuted righteous one
subtitle: Wisdom 2 → Passion narratives
summary: Wisdom 2 describes the hostility directed toward a righteous man who claims a special relationship with God. Edition 1 maps several of these verses to Passion material, making this a high-value passage cluster for close comparison.
items: Compare the claim to divine sonship and the mockery directed at the righteous sufferer.
A source-supported Douay-Rheims relationship; compare the challenge that God should rescue the righteous one.
Compare testing/mockery motifs in the Passion.
A broader righteous-sufferer relationship extending beyond the Gospel Passion scene.

title: Wisdom lived: Sirach, Matthew, and James
subtitle: Sirach → Jesus’ moral teaching → James
summary: Sirach is the densest Deuterocanonical bridge to Matthew and James in Edition 1. This path focuses on speech, humility, testing, charity, correction, and practical righteousness—the moral world in which Christian faith is lived.
items: Compare the discipline of listening and speech.
Compare testing/trial as part of fidelity to God.
Compare responsibility for sin and the denial that God causes temptation.
A Douay-Rheims relationship connecting moral fault and speech.
A source-supported path concerning willing/generous giving.

title: Martyrdom, resurrection, and fidelity
subtitle: 2 Maccabees → Hebrews / Paul / Revelation
summary: 2 Maccabees supplies a rich pre-Christian setting for martyrdom, resurrection hope, fidelity under persecution, and actions concerning the dead. Edition 1 identifies several NT comparison points, many of which remain scholar-review items.
items: Compare Eleazar’s martyrdom setting with Hebrews’ memory of sufferers who refuse release in hope of a better resurrection.
Both passages place actions involving the dead within a resurrection context; the precise relationship requires scholarly judgment.
Compare fidelity unto death and eschatological reward.
A liturgical/festival imagery comparison preserved for review.

title: Tobit and the Gospel moral world
subtitle: Tobit → Matthew / Luke / Acts
summary: Tobit combines prayer, almsgiving, marriage, burial of the dead, angelic ministry, providence, and healing. This path surfaces Edition 1 links into the Gospel and apostolic moral world without claiming that every parallel is a direct literary dependency.
items: Compare prayer and almsgiving as acts remembered before God.
Compare doxological language concerning God’s kingship.
A time/fulfillment comparison preserved for review.

title: Heavenly worship, angels, and apocalyptic imagery
subtitle: Deuterocanon → Revelation
summary: Revelation has a notable network of Edition 1 relationships with the Deuterocanonical books. This path gathers representative examples concerning heavenly signs, worship, judgment, martyrdom, and angelic imagery.
items: The hidden Ark tradition is compared with the Ark appearing in the heavenly temple.
Kingship language in an apocalyptic setting.
A comparison involving silence and divine action.
